title: The Final Experiment

beats.narrativeText: Atlas delivers news unlike anything in the previous sixteen missions: one of the expedition's experiments was never finished.
Every other investigation so far came with a method already worked out. This one doesn't — no detailed instructions for it survive anywhere in the archive.
The learner has to define the investigation themselves and form a prediction, drawing on everything learned across the entire campaign to do it.
Planning the fair test makes something clear fast: this investigation runs entirely on the learner's own reasoning, with nobody supplying the next step.
The learner must collect evidence and analyse the results with no step-by-step guidance — Atlas is there for safety, not for answers.
The expedition's final, unfinished investigation is complete — finished not by the original team, but by the learner who followed their evidence all the way there.
The learner reflects honestly on the investigation's limitations — what a second attempt would do differently, and why that's worth admitting rather than glossing over.
Something has changed that's bigger than this one investigation: the learner isn't just completing investigations designed by someone else anymore. They're designing their own.

activities.title: Define the Investigation
activities.storyContext: One experiment remains unfinished, and no detailed instructions survive for it — the question itself is now the learner's to define.
activities.instructions: Decide exactly what question your investigation will try to answer, and write it down clearly before doing anything else.

activities.title: Form a Prediction
activities.storyContext: A good investigation starts with a prediction to test — not a guess at the answer, but a reasoned expectation you're prepared to be wrong about.
activities.instructions: Form a prediction for what you expect your investigation to show, and explain the reasoning behind it.

activities.title: Plan a Fair Test
activities.storyContext: Atlas provides only safety guidance and procedural reminders — the design is up to the learner.
activities.instructions: Plan a fair test for your investigation, changing only one thing at a time.
activities.output: A plan for a fair test.

activities.title: Collect Evidence
activities.storyContext: Every conclusion needs evidence to support it — especially one nobody else is going to double-check for you this time.
activities.instructions: Carry out your fair test and collect evidence carefully, recording it as you go rather than trying to remember it afterwards.

activities.title: Analyse Results
activities.storyContext: The evidence has to be analysed honestly, whether or not it ends up supporting the prediction you started with.
activities.instructions: Analyse your results and decide whether they genuinely support your prediction — or whether they don't.
activities.output: An analysis of the investigation's results.

activities.title: Reflect on Limitations
activities.storyContext: No investigation is ever completely perfect — admitting that honestly is part of doing good science, not a failure of it.
activities.instructions: Reflect on the limitations of your investigation and what you would genuinely improve if you ran it again.
activities.output: A reflection on the investigation's limitations.

activities.title: Repeat With a Changed Variable
activities.storyContext: Changing one variable can reveal whether your first result was reliable.
activities.instructions: Repeat your investigation with one variable changed, and compare the outcomes.
activities.output: A comparison between the original and repeated investigation.

activities.title: Is Experimental Evidence Reliable?
activities.storyContext: Deciding whether evidence is trustworthy is a core scientific skill.
activities.instructions: Find out how scientists decide whether experimental evidence is reliable.
activities.output: None required — this is an open investigation.

prompts: What would you do differently if you repeated your investigation, and what made you notice that limitation in the first place?

discussionPoints: How did you decide what to test, with no instructions to follow?
What would you do differently if you repeated this investigation?
parentGuide.preparation: Materials will depend on what the learner chooses to investigate — encourage them to plan first, then gather what they need.
parentGuide.assessment: Look for a genuinely fair test (only one thing changed at a time) and honest reflection on the investigation's limitations.

completionCriteria: An investigation defined, a fair test planned, evidence collected, and results analysed.
